findings.title: Scanner status enum writes only open/regression but plan.md documents full six-state lifecycle
findings.detail: plan.md defines the full status lifecycle as 'open|fixing|verifying|fixed|closed|regression' but self-heal-pipeline.md section 'How regression detection slots into /audit-scan' (lines 120-129) shows the scanner writing only 'open' or 'regression' (or dropping). Without a clarifying note, implementers may believe the scanner should write all six states, or that 'fixing'/'verifying'/'fixed' are unreachable. The two sections describe different stages (initial scan vs full lifecycle) but look like contradictions.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a parenthetical note in self-heal-pipeline.md at the scanner output section: '(These are initial states; the full lifecycle — fixing, verifying, fixed, closed — is described in plan.md §schema. The scanner only writes the initial state; /audit-fix transitions status through the remaining states.)'

findings.title: REGRESSION verdict string parsing contract unspecified in self-heal-pipeline
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md specifies the regression detector returns 'REGRESSION:<original_id>:<closing_pr>' but does not specify how this string should be parsed. An implementer might split on ':' to get three parts, or might split on the first colon only. Since AUDIT-IDs contain hyphens but not colons, splitting on ':' works — but this implicit guarantee is undocumented. If an original_id ever contains a colon (e.g., from a future format change), parsing breaks silently.
findings.fix_sketch: Add to the verdict section: 'Parse the REGRESSION verdict by splitting on the first two occurrences of ":" (split limit 3): parts[0]="REGRESSION", parts[1]=original_id, parts[2]=closing_pr. The AUDIT-<repo>-<hash8> format guarantees original_id contains no colons — this invariant must hold for all future ID formats.'

findings.title: closed.json concurrent-write locking is SHOULD not MUST creating data loss risk
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md failure modes table (line 292) acknowledges that concurrent /audit-fix and drafter writes to closed.json can lose a closure: 'if both write simultaneously, last writer wins and one closure may be lost.' The suggested fix uses 'should' for mkdir-based locking — making it optional. Under high-velocity parallel lanes (5+ concurrent), a race is deterministic, not rare, and lost closures mean fingerprint counts are wrong and rules never get drafted.
findings.fix_sketch: Change 'should use mkdir-based locking' to 'MUST use mkdir-based locking' in the failure modes table and add a hard-requirement sentence in the '/audit-fix appends to closed.json' contract section.

findings.title: rubric.json fingerprint_algo missing concat_format separator field
findings.detail: rubric.json specifies normalization rules for each input field (category, file_globs, title) but does not specify how the three normalized values are concatenated before hashing. The self-heal-pipeline.md shows 'sha256(cat|globs|title)' in the lifecycle diagram using '|' as separator, but this is informal ASCII art. Two implementations using different separators (e.g., '|' vs ',' vs '') will produce different fingerprints for the same finding, breaking deduplication.
findings.fix_sketch: Add to rubric.json fingerprint_algo: a 'concat_format' field specifying the exact separator, e.g., '"concat_format": "{category}|{file_globs_joined}|{title}"' where file_globs_joined is the comma-joined sorted globs. Also add a 'test_case' with a known input and expected sha256 hex output.

findings.title: Proposer ranking algorithm has no rule for DUPLICATE status findings
findings.detail: proposer-spec.md section 3 ranking algorithm defines scoring for CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, REGRESSION, COSMETIC findings but makes no mention of DUPLICATE status. The regression-detector is supposed to drop duplicates from the rollup, but if a bug causes a DUPLICATE to appear in index.json, the Proposer has no scoring rule and may either crash or score it incorrectly as IMPORTANT (score 50).
findings.fix_sketch: Add to proposer-spec.md section 3 before the scoring table: 'Pre-filter: drop any finding with status not in [open, regression] before scoring. DUPLICATE findings are supposed to be excluded from index.json by the regression-detector; if any appear, log a warning and skip.'

findings.title: audit-fix closed.json contract describes T2 forward spec without calling it out as such
findings.detail: self-heal-pipeline.md 'How /audit-fix appends to closed.json' (lines 79-109) is written in present tense describing existing behavior, but /audit-fix is a Phase 1/2 deliverable and closed.json writing is a Phase 4 scaffolded feature. The README data flow diagram explicitly notes '[Phase 4 — scaffolded, not yet active; closed.json not written]'. An implementer reading self-heal-pipeline.md without the README would assume the contract describes current behavior.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a callout at the top of the '/audit-fix appends to closed.json' section: '[FORWARD CONTRACT: This describes behavior /audit-fix MUST implement in Phase 4. As of Phase 3 soak, closed.json is not yet written — see README status table. The contract is written prescriptively so T2/T4 implementers have a clear spec.]'

findings.title: PR detection regex lacks case-sensitivity specification for repo name component
findings.detail: plan.md line 126 specifies PR title regex '/AUDIT-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/' which covers mixed case but doesn't state whether matching is case-sensitive. Finding IDs use repo names as-is from the filesystem (e.g., 'IFleet' uppercase, 'factory' lowercase). A case-sensitive match on 'AUDIT-ifleet-xxx' would miss a PR titled 'Fix AUDIT-IFleet-xxx'. The regex character class [A-Za-z0-9_-] is sufficient, but the case-insensitivity contract should be explicit.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a note in plan.md near line 126: 'Match is case-insensitive (/AUDIT-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/i) to tolerate variations in repo name casing. Finding IDs preserve the filesystem directory name case (IFleet vs factory).'

findings.title: README Related section uses absolute /Users/Seb/ paths instead of portable tilde notation
findings.detail: README.md lines 311-313 use absolute paths '/Users/Seb/dev/ai-products/IFleet/ROADMAP.md', '/Users/Seb/.claude/', '/Users/Seb/.omc/splits/'. The rest of the document uses '~/' notation consistently. While there is a note that 'paths below are local filesystem references — they are not clickable links', the absolute paths are platform-specific and inconsistent with the rest of the document.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace all '/Users/Seb/' with '~/' in the Related section. Also update the crontab example in self-heal-pipeline.md which uses '/Users/Seb/.claude/scripts/...' to use '~/.claude/scripts/...'.
